description: Voidborn consciousness vessel. Not a medbay — a mind-bay.
lore:
Named for Plato's concept of recollection — knowledge the soul possessed
before birth — the Anamnesis-class does not heal bodies. It maintains
minds. The ship's neural interface suite can stabilize degrading
consciousness patterns, back up cognitive states, and facilitate transfers
between substrates that the Collective considers routine and other empires
consider existentially terrifying. Patients emerge not just repaired but
clarified, reporting that their thoughts feel "more coherent" afterward.
Whether this means the Anamnesis restores minds or edits them is a
distinction the Collective does not acknowledge.
name: Anamnesis

description: Solarian mining capital. Deploys mining drones autonomously, processes ore on-board. Pinnacle of industrial engineering.
lore: The Automated Extraction Complex represents the pinnacle of Solarian industrial engineering. Ten utility slots — the highest count on any ship in the galaxy — support autonomous mining drone deployment, real-time geological surveying, on-board ore processing, and quality assurance systems that operate without crew intervention. The ship identifies deposits, deploys extraction drones, processes the raw ore into refined materials, and stores the results in the 2,400-unit cargo bay. The entire operation runs autonomously according to algorithms refined over decades of geological research. The Confederacy considers the Automated Extraction Complex its greatest industrial achievement. It is a mining operation in a hull.
name: Automated Extraction Complex

description: Nebula support frigate. Crew wellness is a productivity multiplier.
lore:
The Federation frames the Benefit-class as a humanitarian investment,
but the internal memos are candid: a healthy crew operates at 23%
higher efficiency. Four utility slots accommodate medical bays,
diagnostic systems, and pharmaceutical synthesizers. The double
shields protect a vessel that can't afford to take fire while treating
casualties. Crew insurance premiums drop 30% on fleets that include
a Benefit — which, the Federation points out, makes it pay for itself.
name: Benefit

description: Crimson combat hospital. Patches crews and sends them back into the fight. Triage, not therapy.
lore:
The Cauterizer's name tells you everything about Crimson medical
philosophy: close the wound, stop the bleeding, get them back in
the fight. The five utility slots accommodate medical bays, trauma
systems, and pharmaceutical fabricators optimized for rapid
treatment rather than comprehensive care. Crimson combat medics
train in triage under fire — literally, since the Cauterizer
operates in active combat zones. Two weapon mounts are "standard
Crimson medical equipment" according to fleet procurement. Three
defense slots keep the hospital functional. The cargo hold carries
medical supplies and replacement crew — because the Crimson Fleet
treats both as combat consumables.
name: Cauterizer

description: Crimson assault titan. Takes stations by force. The Fleet's ultimate boarding platform.
lore: The Colossus is the Mace scaled to apocalyptic proportions. A ship designed to physically dock with enemy stations and deliver a small army through breaching systems that can cut through anything short of neutronium. Eight weapon mounts suppress station defenses during approach. The armor is designed to absorb sustained point-blank fire from fixed emplacements. The boarding capacity can seize and hold a medium-sized station in a single operation. Building a Colossus is a statement of intent — the Crimson Fleet doesn't build one unless it plans to take something worth taking. And the Crimson Fleet always plans to take something worth taking.
name: Crimson Colossus

description: Crimson weaponized gas processor. Refines volatiles into fuel, explosives, and chemical weapons components.
lore:
The Gas Cracker-class refines volatile gases into three categories
the Crimson Fleet cares about: fuel for the fleet, explosives for
ordnance, and chemical components for weapons systems. The refinery
processes run at temperatures and pressures that violate every other
empire's safety standards, which the Fleet considers a competitive
advantage. Two weapon mounts protect gas processing operations in
contested nebulae — the Fleet learned that losing a full cargo of
refined volatiles to a pirate raid is more expensive than the guns.
name: Crimson Gas Cracker

description: Crimson siege titan. Long-range planetary bombardment. The war-ender.
lore: The Oblivion exists because some problems don't yield to conventional force. Nine weapon mounts optimized for long-range bombardment deliver ordnance from distances that put the ship beyond effective return fire. The power grid — the largest ever installed in a Crimson vessel — sustains continuous bombardment capable of reducing stations to wreckage and planetary defenses to memories. The Oblivion sacrifices hull and shield for raw firepower: it's not built to take hits, it's built to ensure the enemy never gets the chance to deliver them. The Crimson Fleet has built three Oblivions in its history. That was enough. The word "oblivion" is now a verb in Crimson Fleet tactical lexicon.
name: Crimson Oblivion

description: Solarian ice research platform. Precision cryo-extraction identifies compounds others destroy.
lore:
The Cryo Laboratory-class treats ice extraction as materials science.
Thermal regulators maintain extraction zones at precisely controlled
temperatures, allowing crystallographic analysis to identify and
isolate rare compounds that brute-force ice breaking destroys. The
seven utility slots accommodate instruments that other empires would
mount in a planetary laboratory — the Confederacy considers this the
minimum standard for serious cryo-extraction work. Processing is
slower than competitors but yields compounds that other ships cannot
produce at all.
name: Cryo Laboratory

description: Voidborn anomalous ice harvester. Phase-shifts through ice to extract materials from deep cores.
lore:
The Cryo Phaser-class harvests ice through dimensional phase-shifting
at capital scale. The extraction system reaches through the surface of
ice bodies without disturbing them, pulling target materials directly
from deep cores that conventional equipment cannot access. Nine hundred
shield points protect against the dimensional stress of sustained
phase-extraction operations. The technique is unique to the Voidborn —
other empires lack the dimensional technology to reach into solid
matter without breaking it. The Collective considers this approach
both more efficient and more respectful of the ice body's structural
integrity.
name: Cryo Phaser

description: Solarian precision mining capital. The most methodical extraction system in the galaxy.
lore:
The Deep Core Platform represents the Confederacy's conviction that
mining is applied geology at industrial scale. Eight utility slots
accommodate the most comprehensive geological analysis suite ever
mounted on a mining vessel — real-time seismic modeling, spectral
tomography, and core sample analysis that maps every ore deposit in
an asteroid before the first laser fires. The result is extraction
yields that approach theoretical maximums. One thousand six hundred eighty cargo capacity
holds the results of operations that take longer but waste nothing.
Solarian mining doctrine: the richest ore is the ore you don't leave
behind.
name: Deep Core Platform

description: Heavy mining platform with impressive capacity.
lore: The Deeprock Harvester is a mobile mining operation. These massive vessels can strip an asteroid field in hours, but their slow speed makes them vulnerable. Smart captains hire escorts.
name: Deeprock Harvester

description: Voidborn mining capital. Extracts resources from parallel dimensional layers. Harvests ore, gas, and ice simultaneously.
lore:
The Dimensional Harvester-class extracts resources from parallel
dimensional layers that other empires cannot perceive, let alone reach.
Two thousand shield points protect against dimensional stress during
sustained multi-layer extraction operations. Nine utility slots
accommodate the most advanced sensor and extraction systems the
Collective has ever produced. The Harvester can extract ore, gas, and
ice simultaneously from overlapping dimensional layers — a capability
unique to this vessel. The Collective claims the Dimensional Harvester
"accelerates resource regeneration" in depleted fields by pulling
matter through dimensional rifts. Other empires' physicists consider
this claim impossible. The resources appear anyway.
name: Dimensional Harvester

description: Solid mid-tier mining vessel with better defenses.
lore:
The Drillship bridges the gap between hobby miner and professional.
Its reinforced hull can take a few hits, and the expanded utility
slots allow for better mining equipment or defensive modules.
name: Drillship

description: Outer Rim field medic vessel. Keeps crews alive using improvisation and stubbornness.
lore:
Frontier medicine is creative medicine. The Duct Tape Special carries
medical supplies, fabrication tools, and enough spare parts to patch
up ships and crews in deep space where the nearest hospital is three
jumps away. Rim medics are famously resourceful — "it's sterile enough"
is a professional assessment, not a complaint. The speed ensures quick
arrival at disaster sites, and the life support systems are the one
thing on the ship that actually meets manufacturer specifications.
name: Duct Tape Special

description: Nebula convoy guard. Protects high-value shipments on a per-engagement basis.
lore:
The Escort-class exists because the Federation did the math: hiring
mercenary escorts costs 12% more per annum than fielding purpose-built
convoy guards. Two weapon mounts and enough speed to intercept raiders
make the Escort a cost-effective deterrent. The Federation markets it
as "insurance with teeth."
name: Escort

description: Dedicated mining vessel with enhanced ore storage.
lore:
The Excavator represents the next step up for serious miners. Its
expanded cargo hold and multiple utility slots make extended mining
operations practical, though you'll want an escort in dangerous space.
name: Excavator

description: Outer Rim dreadnought. Named for the boundary. Built to cross it.
lore:
Named for the First Step incident — the moment Outer Rim scouts reached
the galaxy's uncharted boundary and stopped, for the first and only time,
because something stopped them. The First Step-class is designed to go
back. Speed 2 on a capital hull is unheard of, achieved through engine
arrays that consume fuel at rates other empires consider wasteful. The
1000-unit fuel reserve ensures the range to reach whatever lies beyond
the boundary. Seven weapon mounts ensure that whatever stopped the scouts
will face a different reception this time. Whether the Rim actually
intends to build enough First Steps to try is a question their admirals
answer only with smiles.
name: First Step

description: Solarian precision gas refinery. Fractional distillation with scientific accuracy. Best yield ratios.
lore:
The Fractional Distillery-class separates gas mixtures with laboratory-
grade precision at industrial scale. Seven utility slots support
spectrometers, composition analyzers, and fractional separation columns
that sort gas streams by molecular weight, reactivity, and commercial
value simultaneously. The Confederacy's gas processing doctrine
maximizes value extraction from every cubic meter of collected gas —
compounds that other empires vent as waste, the Distillery isolates
and stores as premium products. Processing quality is the highest in
the galaxy because the Confederacy considers anything less to be
unprofessional.
name: Fractional Distillery

description: Nebula bulk gas collection and compression vessel. Enormous intake, stores compressed gas for transport.
lore:
The Gas Compressor-class was designed by the same Federation accounting
department that produces all their best ships. Enormous intake scoops
channel gas into compression tanks that store collected gas at densities
other empires' safety regulators would reject. One thousand twenty
cargo capacity carries both raw and compressed gas — the Federation
hauls everything and lets the station-side brokers sort out pricing.
Unarmed because guns don't generate revenue. The Gas Compressor doesn't
care about purity or processing — it cares about volume, and it has
more of it than anyone.
name: Gas Compressor

description: Outer Rim jury-rigged gas processor. Fast throughput, rough processing, doesn't care about purity.
lore:
The Gas Cracker burns through gas clouds at speed, collection scoops
wide open, processing systems running flat out. Purity standards are
"whatever comes out the other end." The Rim's gas refineries prioritize
throughput over quality — five hundred cargo of roughly-processed gas
is worth more than two hundred cargo of pristine fractions when you're
supplying frontier fuel depots. Speed 2 lets the Gas Cracker follow
gas clouds as they drift, maintaining continuous collection without
the repositioning delays that slow competitors.
name: Gas Cracker

description: Outer Rim mobile base. A station that got tired of sitting still.
lore: The Here to Stay-class is what the Rim builds when it wants to plant a flag somewhere and make it stick. Part command post, part supply depot, part repair facility, part community center — it's a mobile station for frontier settlements too new or too stubborn for permanent infrastructure. It moves at speed 1, which by Rim standards is practically stationary, but the hull is the toughest thing the Rim has ever built. When a Here to Stay arrives in a system, it means the Rim isn't just visiting. The name isn't a description — it's a promise.
name: Here to Stay

description: Crimson thermal lance ice platform. Brute-force cracking with military-grade systems.
lore:
The Ice Fortress-class applies military-grade thermal systems to ice
extraction and processing at capital scale. The thermal lances operate
at temperatures that liquify ice formations in seconds, and the
refinery systems separate the resulting melt into fuel components,
coolant, and rare crystalline materials. The Fleet needs coolant for
weapon systems, fuel for fleet operations, and the Ice Fortress
produces both in quantities that keep a battle group operational
indefinitely. The hull armor doubles as thermal shielding — the
extraction systems generate enough waste heat to damage nearby ships.
name: Ice Fortress

description: Nebula industrial ice harvester-hauler. Carves entire ice asteroids and hauls them whole.
lore:
The Ice Logistics-class approaches frozen resources the way the
Federation approaches everything: as a supply chain problem. The
ship's tractor systems carve entire ice bodies free from asteroid
fields and secure them in the cavernous cargo bay for transport to
processing facilities. Why refine in the field when station-side
facilities do it better? Nine hundred sixty cargo capacity carries ice
in bulk — whole chunks, minimally processed, maximum volume. The
cryo-containment systems maintain cargo at extraction temperature,
preventing melt loss that the Federation considers an unacceptable
hit to the profit margin.
name: Ice Logistics

description: Outer Rim improvised ice platform. Welded-together saws, heaters, and cargo pods. Ugly but effective.
lore:
The Ice Rig looks exactly like what it is: industrial ice saws,
thermal heaters, and cargo pods welded onto a hull frame with
structural bracing that a Solarian engineer would condemn. It works.
Speed 2 gets it to ice fields before competitors, the saws cut
chunks free fast, the heaters crack them into manageable pieces, and
the cargo pods hold seven hundred and eighty units of roughly-processed
ice product. Refinement quality is "adequate." The Rim doesn't have
time for precision cryo-extraction — the frontier needs coolant and
fuel, and the Ice Rig delivers both.
name: Ice Rig

description: Solarian construction platform. Capital-scale mobile shipyard and engineering base.
lore: A magnum opus is an artist's greatest work, and the Magnum Opus-class is the Confederacy's greatest feat of engineering — a ship that builds other ships. Eight utility slots support fabrication bays, material processing arrays, and precision assembly systems. The onboard construction AI follows blueprints with sub-millimeter accuracy and refuses to proceed if any component fails to meet specification. Construction projects are accompanied by progress reports issued on the hour. The vessel's own construction took nine years and generated more technical documentation than some civilizations produce in a century.
name: Magnum Opus

description: Nebula mega ore hauler. Obscene cargo capacity. Empties asteroid belts and hauls everything to market.
lore:
The Mega Hauler-class exists because the Federation asked "what if we
just... carried more?" Two thousand one hundred sixty cargo capacity is achieved
through structural engineering that other empires consider irresponsible
— the cargo bay occupies over 60% of the hull volume. Zero weapon
mounts because the Federation considers guns on a mining platform a
waste of cargo space. Escorts exist for a reason, and ore in the hold
generates revenue that guns never will. The Mega Hauler doesn't mine
efficiently — it mines thoroughly, stripping asteroid belts down to
pebbles and hauling everything to market in a single trip.
name: Mega Hauler

description: Solarian freighter. Efficient cargo management with extensive monitoring.
lore:
Every gram of cargo in a Meridian-class freighter is tracked by seven
independent inventory systems. The manifest reconciliation process runs
continuously, comparing predicted mass distribution against actual sensor
readings. Smuggling aboard a Meridian is technically possible but requires
defeating more auditing software than most planetary tax authorities employ.
name: Meridian

description: Outer Rim mining capital. An entire mining operation welded onto a jump drive. Ugly, stubborn, effective.
lore: The Mobile Mining Base is an entire mining operation welded onto a jump drive. Held together by structural bracing, duct tape, and frontier stubbornness. At 350,000 credits it's the cheapest T5 industrial vessel by a wide margin, because the Rim builds capital ships the same way it builds everything: from whatever's available. Twenty-six hundred and forty cargo capacity hauls everything a remote mining operation produces. Two weapon mounts because the frontier is the frontier, and mining bases attract pirates. The Mobile Mining Base can operate independently for extended periods — no station docking required. It is, in every sense, a self-contained mining colony that happens to have engines.
name: Mobile Mining Base

description: Nebula construction titan. Builds stations, shipyards, and the future of Federation commerce.
lore:
The Foundation-class is the Federation's largest construction platform,
capable of assembling entire stations from raw materials in the field.
960 units of cargo capacity store prefabricated components, and eight
utility slots support fabrication arrays, structural scanners, and
project coordination systems. Where a Foundation parks, a new chapter
of Federation commerce begins. The three weapon mounts are described
as "site security" — because a half-built station full of rare
materials attracts unwanted attention.
name: Nebula Foundation

description: Nebula luxury titan. The ultimate expression of commercial supremacy.
lore:
The Sovereign-class is the single most expensive vessel the Federation
produces, and it is designed to make sure everyone knows it. Gold-laced
circuitry, crystal viewports spanning entire decks, and shields that
could weather a fleet engagement protect an interior that makes orbital
palaces look modest. Six defense slots ensure the investment survives
anything short of a coordinated capital assault. The Federation builds
exactly one per fiscal quarter, and the waiting list is longer than
some empires' ship registries.
name: Nebula Sovereign

description: Outer Rim jury-rigged gas processor. Fast throughput, rough processing, doesn't care about purity.
lore:
The Gas Cracker burns through gas clouds at speed, collection scoops
wide open, processing systems running flat out. Purity standards are
"whatever comes out the other end." The Rim's gas refineries prioritize
throughput over quality — five hundred cargo of roughly-processed gas
is worth more than two hundred cargo of pristine fractions when you're
supplying frontier fuel depots. Speed 2 lets the Gas Cracker follow
gas clouds as they drift, maintaining continuous collection without
the repositioning delays that slow competitors.
name: Outer Rim Gas Cracker

description: Solarian medical cruiser. Full hospital capabilities with research-grade facilities.
lore:
The Panacea-class is a fully accredited hospital ship with research
capabilities that rival most planetary medical centers. Four independent
life support units maintain separate sterile environments for surgical,
recovery, quarantine, and research operations. The medical AI holds
honorary degrees from three Solarian universities and maintains a
diagnostic accuracy rate the Confederacy Medical Board describes as
"statistically indistinguishable from perfect." Patients receive a
comprehensive discharge summary whether they want one or not.
name: Panacea

description: Voidborn exotic gas processor. Extracts gases from dimensional rifts that other ships can't detect.
lore:
The Phase Condenser-class extracts gases from dimensional rifts that
other empires' sensors cannot detect. The collection membranes extend
into adjacent dimensional layers, capturing exotic compounds that
exist only at the boundary between realities. The condensation process
forces these inter-dimensional gases into normal-space stable states,
producing materials with properties that conventional chemistry cannot
explain. Seven utility slots support the phase-detection and
stabilization equipment needed to operate safely — "safely" being
a relative term when harvesting matter from between dimensions.
name: Phase Condenser

description: Voidborn consciousness nexus. A mobile node of the Collective's shared mind.
lore:
Named for the Gnostic concept of divine fullness, the Pleroma-class
is the ultimate expression of Voidborn collective consciousness. It
does not merely coordinate a fleet — it networks the minds of every
Voidborn ship and crew member in a system into a single distributed
intelligence. Ships docked with the Pleroma report their systems
operating at efficiencies that exceed individual specifications.
Crews experience a state the Collective calls "convergence" — a
temporary dissolution of individual perspective into shared awareness.
Non-Voidborn observers describe the effect as "an entire fleet
becoming one organism." The Collective considers this description
imprecise. The Pleroma is not the fleet becoming one organism.
It is the fleet remembering that it always was.
name: Pleroma

description: A humble mining vessel for new pilots. Slow but reliable.
lore:
The Prospector is where every pilot's journey begins. Originally designed
as an automated ore collector, these reliable workhorses have served
generations of miners. What they lack in speed and firepower, they make
up for in durability and low maintenance.
name: Prospector

description: Voidborn harmonic extractor. Vibrates ore out of asteroids through dimensional frequency matching.
lore:
The Resonance-class mining vessel operates on a principle that Voidborn
engineers describe as "sympathetic frequency extraction" and everyone
else describes as "impossible." The ship generates a harmonic field that
causes ore deposits to separate from their surrounding matrix without
physical contact. Asteroids subjected to Resonance-class operations
develop unusual geometric patterns in their remaining structure. The
Collective considers these patterns aesthetically pleasing. Other
miners consider them evidence that something profoundly unnatural
has occurred.
name: Resonance

description: Voidborn resonance excavation platform. Vibrates ore free through dimensional harmonics at capital scale.
lore:
The Resonance Array-class extends Voidborn harmonic extraction to
capital scale. The dimensional frequency generators vibrate entire
asteroid fields at their resonant frequency, separating ore from rock
across multiple targets simultaneously. Nine hundred shield points
protect against resonance feedback — when you vibrate asteroids at
frequencies that shouldn't exist, the universe occasionally objects.
Eight utility slots accommodate the sensor arrays, harmonic tuners,
and dimensional stabilizers needed for safe operation. The Collective
insists the process is "cooperative" rather than "destructive." The
asteroids have not been asked for comment.
name: Resonance Array

description: Outer Rim overbuilt mining platform. Fast for its size, cheap, strips belts bare.
lore:
The Rock Crusher is the only T4 mining platform with speed 2 — the
overclocked engines are technically out of spec, but they work, and
the Rim doesn't believe in specs anyway. Eighteen hundred cargo capacity
means it strips belts bare before slower competitors finish their
first load. At 85,000 credits, it's the cheapest T4 miner available
because the Rim builds ships from whatever's available rather than
whatever's optimal. The single weapon mount exists because frontier
mining operations attract attention, and the Rim's response to
attention is always armed.
name: Rock Crusher

description: Outer Rim mining platform. Several previous owners. Currently operational. No questions about the welds.
lore:
The Rubble-class is what the Patchwork builds when it doesn't have the
components to build anything better. The mining laser is original
equipment. The hull is a composite of three different ship frames that
happened to fit. The cargo hold has a slight lean to port that the
previous owner described as "character." It mines ore. That is the
complete list of things it does. For most Rim pilots, that's enough.
name: Rubble

description: Nebula construction vessel. Builds the infrastructure that generates the revenue.
lore: The Scaffold-class is the Federation's mid-range construction platform, deployed wherever a new station, altais, or fuel depot needs building. Unarmed because the Federation would rather spend the tonnage on building materials than guns. Five utility slots support fabrication arrays, structural integrity monitors, and project management systems. Every station the Scaffold builds becomes a new node in the Federation's trade network — a capital investment with compound returns.
name: Scaffold

description: Outer Rim mining vessel. Ugly but effective. Practically indestructible through redundancy.
lore:
The Scrapheap looks like someone welded three different ships together
and added a mining laser. That's because that's exactly what happened.
Rim engineers discovered that by combining redundant systems from
multiple wrecks, you get a ship where nothing works perfectly but
everything has a backup. When the primary power coupling fails, the
secondary (from a Solarian shuttle) takes over. When that fails, the
tertiary (from gods-know-what) kicks in. It's not elegant. It works.
name: Scrapheap

description: Disposable Crimson boarding craft. Gets marines to the target hull. Everything after that is their problem.
lore:
The Shiv has no weapons because it IS the weapon. Twelve tons of
tungsten-reinforced prow designed to breach hull plating and deliver
a boarding party directly into the enemy ship's interior. The design
is deliberately cheap — Crimson Fleet accountants classify Shivs as
ammunition, not vessels. The armor rating is excellent for its size
because the entire ship is essentially armor wrapped around a cockpit
and a marine compartment. No weapons, minimal fuel, maximum speed
toward the target. Shiv pilots either become heroes or statistics,
and the Crimson Fleet honors both.
name: Shiv

description: Crimson mobile weapons factory. Mines, smelts, and produces ordnance in one terrifying hull.
lore: The Siege Foundry combines mining, smelting, and munitions production into one hull. Feed it asteroids, and the internal forges turn raw ore into ammunition, weapon components, and replacement parts. Three weapon mounts on a T5 industrial ship — more guns than most dedicated warships two tiers below. The hull — 2,500 points backed by 120 armor — is built to sustain operations in hostile space indefinitely. The Crimson Fleet designed the Siege Foundry to operate behind enemy lines: mine local resources, produce ordnance, and keep fighting without ever returning to a supply base. A mobile weapons factory that turns asteroids into ordnance. The galaxy has not yet determined whether this is brilliant or terrifying. The Crimson Fleet considers it both.
name: Siege Foundry

description: Crimson armored mining platform. Fortress hull, can fight back. The Fleet's heavy extraction asset.
lore:
The Strip Mine-class is what happens when the Crimson Fleet applies
capital ship engineering to asteroid mining. Twelve hundred points of
hull and fifty-five points of armor make it nearly indestructible by
anything short of a dedicated assault force. Two weapon mounts mean
the Strip Mine fights back — mining operations in contested space
continue uninterrupted while the weapons handle interruptions. Fourteen
hundred forty cargo capacity fills over sustained extraction operations that
other empires would consider a siege. The Fleet considers the Strip
Mine a strategic asset: it doesn't just mine a system, it claims it.
name: Strip Mine

description: Nebula mobile strip-mining fleet. Obscene cargo capacity. Empties entire asteroid belts.
lore:
Three thousand six hundred cargo capacity. The Strip Miner-class is the Federation's
final answer to the question "how much ore can one ship carry?" The
hull is essentially a collection of cargo bays connected by structural
members and fitted with engines. Zero weapon mounts because every cubic
meter of weapons is a cubic meter of lost revenue. The Strip Miner
arrives at an asteroid belt and doesn't leave until the belt is empty.
Federation logistics planners love it. Safety inspectors are less
enthusiastic about the structural compromises required to fit 3,600
units of cargo into a hull that other empires would allocate a fraction of that.
name: Strip Miner

description: Nebula mobile trade depot. Sets up a marketplace anywhere there's demand.
lore:
The Surplus-class is a marketplace on a hull. Its oversized cargo holds
store inventory for field trading, while the CPU array runs exchange
matching engines, price feeds, and automated market-making algorithms.
Where stations are scarce, a Surplus pilot becomes the economy — setting
prices, filling orders, and taking a cut of every transaction. The
Federation markets the Surplus as "entrepreneurship infrastructure."
Independent traders describe it less charitably as "that guy who shows
up at every mining site with a markup."
name: Surplus

description: Nebula expedition vessel. Deep-space exploration with all the comforts of a corner office.
lore:
The Survey-class is the Federation's answer to the question: "What's
out there that we haven't monetized yet?" Extended fuel reserves for
months-long expeditions, a high-capacity CPU array for mapping and
analysis, and five utility slots for every conceivable survey instrument.
The comfortable crew quarters are a practical decision — well-rested
explorers discover more profitable resources.
name: Survey

description: Solarian medical frigate. Emergency response with diagnostic excellence.
lore:
The Triage-class carries no weapons — the Confederacy considers it a violation
of medical ethics to arm a hospital ship, even in a war zone. What it lacks in
offensive capability, it compensates for with the most comprehensive diagnostic
suite available at its tonnage. The dual life support units maintain separate
environments for patients of different species. The medical AI's bedside
manner has been described as "clinically precise and emotionally theoretical."
name: Triage

description: Nebula mining specialist. Exceptional cargo capacity for extended operations.
lore:
"A Windfall is what happens when preparation meets opportunity." The
Federation's mining vessel outperforms competitors in one metric that
matters most to traders: how much ore you can bring back per trip. The
expanded cargo hold reduces the number of dock-and-sell cycles needed,
which the Federation has calculated saves 15% in time-cost over a
standard mining shift. This statistic is prominently displayed on the
hull, in case potential customers are watching.
name: Windfall
